gtk.title: Pushchairs and buggies
gtk.text: I can’t find any rule against pushchairs, and each big toilet block has baby changing. It’s up to two miles end to end, so I would bring one, but leave camping trolleys at home as every bag is searched.

gtk.title: Dogs
gtk.text: Dogs aren’t allowed on the showground, because of the noise, the heat and the hot ground on a working airfield. The rules I read don’t agree on assistance dogs, so I would call Customer Services on 01285 713456 if this affects you.

gtk.title: Your own food and drink
gtk.text: You can bring your own food and drink, but no barbecues anywhere on site. I couldn’t find a clear rule on bringing your own alcohol, so I would check before you pack any.

gtk.title: Gazebos, windbreaks and chairs
gtk.text: Folding chairs and blankets are fine. Shelters and step ladders up to 1.5 metres are allowed, but not within 10 metres of the crowd line, and full height gazebos and tents aren’t allowed.

gtk.title: Water refill points
gtk.text: There are free water bowsers at each refuelling station and around the showground. I would bring a refillable bottle, or you can buy one from the merch units.

gtk.title: Changing Places toilet
gtk.text: I haven’t seen a Changing Places toilet confirmed, but there’s a High Dependency Unit toilet in the Restricted Mobility Viewing Area. Bring your RADAR key if you have one, and I would call Customer Services first.

gtk.title: Carers' tickets
gtk.text: Blue Badge holders and Access Card holders with the +1 symbol can ask for a free carer ticket, but conditions apply. Book it by phone, not online, and it doesn’t cover Park and View days.

gtk.title: Hearing support (hearing loops, BSL, deaf visitors)
gtk.text: I haven’t seen hearing loops or BSL confirmed. The Access Card can flag that you need help with auditory information, and the commentary is on Airtattoo LIVE, 87.7FM, so I would call Customer Services before you go.

gtk.title: Quiet area (a calm or sensory space)
gtk.text: If you need a break, ask at the Central Information Point and they’ll take you to the Wellness Room. Just bear in mind nowhere on an airfield is fully quiet once the flying starts.

gtk.title: Re-entry (can you leave and come back)
gtk.text: Tickets are valid for a single entry only. I would pack everything you need for the day, and use the free Drop Zone for anything heavy.

gtk.title: First aid and lost children
gtk.text: The first aid post is next to the blue customer entry point, and lost children are looked after at the Central Visitor Information Point. I would pick up a free wristband for each child when you arrive.

gtk.title: If it rains
gtk.text: Unfortunately the weather on the day will be what it will be, so plan accordingly. If it’s fresh, dress in layers to keep warm. The refuelling stations have some shelter, and a changed programme doesn’t mean a refund.

days.html:
Pick Your Day

RIAT runs over three days, and they aren’t all the same. Saturday and Sunday have the full display and the whole showground open. Friday is shorter and quieter, with fewer tickets. Have a think about who’s coming and what you’re after, and I’ll suggest the day I would pick.

Friday 16 JulyOpen 07:30 to 18:00, with a highlights display from 11:00 to 15:00. Fewer tickets and a lower price. Part of the showground is closed while aircraft are still arriving for the static park.
Saturday 17 JulyOpen 07:30 to 19:30, with flying from 10:00 to 17:30. The whole showground is open, and the Family Enclosure runs today and Sunday.
Sunday 18 JulyOpen 07:30 to 19:30, with flying from 10:00 to 17:30. The same full display as Saturday, and the only day for the Lightning Pavilion.
Either sideArrivals on Wednesday and Thursday, departures on Monday, but only from Park and View. See .

Who’s coming?

What are you after?

Anything else?

I Would Pick The Friday

  1. WhyIt’s a shorter day with fewer people, and some acts are picked for Friday that may not fly at the weekend. You also see more aircraft arriving after the display.
  2. Good to knowThe flying runs 11:00 to 15:00 and part of the showground is closed. Tickets are limited, so I would book early.
  3. Getting thereCar parks open at 06:00, and parking still has to be booked ahead. See .

I Would Pick The Saturday

  1. WhyYou get more than seven hours of flying and the whole showground open. If the weather is poor, you still have Sunday to try again, as long as you can get a ticket.
  2. Good to knowThe Family Enclosure runs on Saturday and Sunday, with shade, seating and baby changing. See .
  3. Getting thereCar parks open at 06:00 and gates at 07:30. I would arrive early and save your pitch first.

I Would Pick The Sunday

  1. WhyIt’s the same full display as Saturday, and it suits you if you want to stay on for the departures on Monday from Park and View.
  2. Good to knowThe Lightning Pavilion only runs on Sunday. Monday Park and View was already sold out when I last checked, so book soon if you want it.
  3. Getting thereCar parks open at 06:00 and gates at 07:30. Parking and the shuttle buses must be booked ahead.
Jack’s tipIf you’re not sure, I would go for Saturday. It gives you the full show and a spare day if the weather goes against you. Weekend and multi day tickets are sold too, and this might work for your family if you’re camping nearby.

Times are for RIAT27. Prices and what’s open on Friday may change.

ground.html:
The Ground Show

RIAT is huge on the ground as well as in the air. The showground runs for up to two miles along the runway, so I would pick one end to start from rather than trying to see it all at once. Take a look at the map flags as you go, and you won’t get lost.

CostIncluded in entry
GatesOpen 07:30
Static parkOn hard standing
Getting aboutFree bus round the site

How I Would Do It

  1. Save your pitch firstIf you want a front row seat, head to the crowd line as soon as you’re in and set up. Then the ground show is yours until 10:00.
  2. Walk the static parkIt’s quietest first thing. Take a look around the aircraft and speak to the crews while they have time to chat.
  3. Stalls, zones and foodVisit the trade stalls and the zones, then check the food options before the lunchtime queues build.
  4. Toilet before the flyingI would go before the flying display starts. If you aren’t waiting to see a particular display later, use it as a toilet break.

Things To See

Included

The Static Park

Aircraft from air forces around the world, parked on hard standing so it’s easy to walk round. For 2027, keep an eye out for the tiger striped jets of the Tiger Gathering.

Included

Take A Look Inside

Some aircraft are opened up for you to take a look inside, and children love a peek inside a giant transport. You can also buy exclusive merch in or outside some of the aircraft.

Included

Techno Zone

Over 40 hands on exhibits. Power Up! has pilot VR, drone simulators and cyber challenges, and Engineers Of Tomorrow is full of building challenges, both aimed at ages 5 to 18. There are talks on the Inspire Stage too.

Included

RAF Experience

A team of around 200 RAF people ready to talk about their training, their jobs and their kit. It’s the place to go if anyone in your group is thinking about joining. More on the RAF Village is in the .

Pay as you go

Take Off Zone

At the eastern end, with pilot meet and greets, street food and a double decker bus bar with a view of the flying from the top deck. Aircrew Trading next door sells air force memorabilia from several countries.

Pay as you go

Stalls And Crafts

Kiosks selling handmade jewellery, vintage fashion, art, ceramics and military surplus. I would leave your shopping in the free Drop Zone at the central information point, so you aren’t carrying it all day.

From £12

Official Merch And Programme

The main megastore is in the centre, with tented shops on the showground and trailers at each entry point. When I last checked, the programme was £12 bought with your ticket or £15 at the show. Spotters love the Aircraft Checklist, sold in the same places.

Finding Your Way

Orange flagsYour location number
Navy flagsNearby food, toilets and zones
Information pointsEast, central and west
FridayPart of the site is closed
Jack’s tipI would do the static park first thing and save the Techno Zone for a gap in the flying, when the kids need a break from the noise. Your child’s ears are delicate, so try to protect them as much as possible, and bring your own ear defenders as RIAT doesn’t hire them out.

skipped.flights: RIAT doesn’t offer pleasure, helicopter, warbird or balloon flights at or from RAF Fairford, and visiting aircraft are limited to display sponsors and VIPs.
skipped.support: It’s a ticketed show, so there’s nothing to keep free.

notes: 1) Dogs and assistance dogs: the official Accessibility FAQ answers the assistance dog question with 'dogs are not permitted on the showground' (https://www.airtattoo.com/faqs/accessibility/), but the Ticket T&Cs Key Points still say assistance dogs are exempt (https://www.airtattoo.com/terms-and-conditions/ticket-tcs-key-points). The page says no dogs, which is safe, but it may be worth a line telling assistance dog users to call 01285 713456. 2) The page puts the Wellness Room 'near mile marker 34'; the official accessibility page just says to ask at the Central Information Point to be taken there (https://www.airtattoo.com/the-airshow/plan-your-visit/accessibilitydisabled/). 3) The Vintage Village is mentioned on the page (Food and facilities) but doesn't appear in the official The Experience pages at the moment; worth checking once the RIAT27 attractions are announced. 4) The official Show Info Hub is still a 'check back closer to the show' placeholder for RIAT27, and the showground map is the 2025 one, so the ground section is based on the current zone pages. 5) The official Friday Futures FAQ says a fully quiet or low sensory area isn't possible on the main site, so I kept the quiet area tile honest about that. 6) Friday ticket price isn't published, only that it's discounted compared with Saturday and Sunday.
